newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian communist warns of possible civil war.
newsitem.headline: Russian communist warns of possible civil war.

text.p: Russian Communist Party leader Gennady Zyuganov on Thursday said civil war could break out if top government and Kremlin officials were allowed to continue vying openly for power, Interfax news agency reported.

Zyuganov said the increasingly bitter fight between security chief Alexander Lebed and Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov "could end in a general civil war as well as destroying the army", the agency said.
Kulikov dramatically increased the stakes on Wednesday by accusing Lebed of preparing to use force to seize power, a charge his rival dismissed.

"The country is once again being pushed towards events of the kind it experienced in August 1991 and October 1993," Zyuganov said, referring to an abortive coup by Soviet officials and a conflict between President Boris Yeltsin and hardliners.

Zyuganov, who has kept a low profile since losing to Yeltsin in the second round of the presidential election in July, said he was prepared to do all he could to help stabilise Russia and called on the army not to let itself be provoked.
Zyuganov gained 40 percent of the vote in July, but he knows that he would probably lose a straight contest with Lebed in a future presidential poll.
